parameters.content:
## Monitor contractor licences and get a Slack alert 30 days before one expires

![Workflow overview](https://scrapebench.dev/img/n8n/license-expiration-monitor/canvas.png)

> **Self-hosted only.** This template uses the `@apify/n8n-nodes-apify` community node, which cannot be installed on n8n Cloud.

### Who's it for
Anyone who keeps a standing list of contractors rather than a one-off list: insurance agents with a book of contractor clients, general contractors managing an approved-sub list, property managers with a vendor roster, marketplace ops teams admitting trade accounts.

The failure mode this fixes is finding out about a lapsed licence at the worst possible moment - at claim time, at audit, or when a sub is already on site.

### What it does
Every Monday it re-checks each contractor on your roster against that state's licensing board and sends **one** Slack digest, grouped worst-first:

- `EXPIRED` - the licence lapsed
- `STATUS CHANGED` - it is no longer what you recorded (revoked, suspended, inactive)
- `EXPIRING` - it lapses within 30 days
- `COULD NOT CHECK` - the lookup itself failed, so that licence was **not** checked
- `SEVERAL LICENCES MATCH` - the name hit more than one licence, so nothing is guessed
- `NO MATCH AT THE PORTAL` - the lookup ran and the board had no record for that name
- `NO EXPIRY PUBLISHED` - that state does not publish an expiry for this licence

Rows that are active and not expiring produce no message at all. `COULD NOT CHECK` exists on purpose: a monitor that goes quiet when a lookup breaks is worse than no monitor, because silence reads as "everything is fine".

Covers 17 states: AL, AR, CA, CT, FL, MA, MI, MN, NC, NM, NV, OR, SC, TN, TX, VA, WA. Contractors in the other 33 are passed through labelled, never dropped and never reported as unlicensed.

### How to set up
1. Install the `@apify/n8n-nodes-apify` community node.
2. Add your Apify API key as an Apify credential on the **Look up the licence** node.
3. Replace the **Your roster** node with your own source - Google Sheets, Airtable, Postgres, a CRM. Each row needs `company` and a 2-letter `state`; `license_number` is optional and makes the lookup exact.
4. Add your Slack credential to **Send the digest to Slack**, pick a channel, and enable the node. It ships disabled so the workflow runs on import without one.

### Requirements
- An Apify account and API token (the lookups cost about $0.004 each)
- A Slack credential, if you want the digest delivered
- Self-hosted n8n (community node)

### How to customize
- **Change the warning window:** `WARN_DAYS` at the top of **Classify each licence**.
- **Change the cadence:** the Schedule Trigger. Daily costs seven times as much as weekly; the data changes slowly, so weekly is usually the right trade.
- **Add a state:** one row in the `ACTORS` map in **Route by state**.
- **Send it somewhere else:** swap the Slack node for email, Teams, or a webhook - it is handed one preformatted `text` field.

## 1. Your roster
Swap this for **Google Sheets -> Get rows**, Airtable, Postgres, or your CRM.

Each row needs:
- `company` - the business or licensee name
- `state` - 2-letter code

`license_number` is optional and makes the lookup exact.

`known_status` is what you recorded last time. Blank on the first run is fine - it just means nothing reads as *changed* yet.

## 2. Route each row to its state's board
One Code node instead of a 17-way Switch. It maps the state to the right Apify actor **and** to that actor's own input field - they are not uniform:

- most take `query`
- New Mexico takes `businessName`
- South Carolina takes `lastName`
- Virginia takes `nameFilter`
- Connecticut goes through the multi-state actor

It also asks for `includeDetails`, because the expiry date lives on the detail record, not the summary row.

## 3. Uncovered states pass through
A contractor outside the 17 covered states is labelled and kept.

Never dropped, never reported as unlicensed. "We didn't look" is not the same as "they aren't licensed".

## 4. What changed since last time
Seven outcomes, worst first. Two of them are the point of the template:

**COULD NOT CHECK** - the lookup itself failed, so nothing was verified. Kept separate from **NO MATCH AT THE PORTAL**, where the lookup worked and the board simply had no record. A monitor that goes silent when it breaks is worse than no monitor, and one that reports a breakage as a portal result is worse still.

**NO EXPIRY PUBLISHED** - not every state publishes one. That is stated plainly instead of being treated as "not expiring".

`WARN_DAYS` sets the 30-day window.

## 5. One message, not twenty
Rows that are active and not expiring never reach here - a quiet week is silence, not an empty digest.

The Slack node ships **disabled** so this template runs on import without a Slack credential. Add yours, pick a channel, enable it.
